tips.title: Jouer à for games, faire de for the rest
tips.body: A sport you **play** with a ball or a board takes **jouer à**: *jouer au foot, au tennis, aux cartes*. Everything else takes **faire de**: *faire du vélo, de la natation, de l'équitation, des randonnées*. Ask "can I play it?" and the verb chooses itself.

tips.title: The contraction happens on its own
tips.body: *À + le* is always **au**, *à + les* is **aux**, *de + le* is **du**, *de + les* is **des**. *La* and *l'* never contract. Writing *à le foot* or *de le vélo* is the most common error in this topic, and it is always wrong.

tips.title: Pour rester en forme
tips.body: *Je fais du sport **pour rester en forme**.* (to stay fit). *Pour* + infinitive gives a reason for doing anything, and *rester en forme* fits every sentence in this topic. *Être en forme* is to be fit; *en bonne santé* is healthy.

tips.title: Fois for times
tips.body: *Deux **fois** par semaine* — twice a week. *Fois* is the word for *times* when counting occasions; *temps* is time in general. *Une fois, deux fois, trois fois par semaine* — and never *deux temps*.

tips.title: Faire is irregular
tips.body: *Je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous **faisons**, vous **faites**, ils **font**.* Three forms break the pattern — *faisons, faites, font* — and this topic uses *faire* constantly, so the whole table needs to be automatic.

why.matters: Sport is the first topic where the small words carry the marks. French splits activities into games you *play*, with *jouer à*, and things you *do*, with *faire de*, and then contracts the little word with the article, so *le foot* becomes *jouer au foot* and *le vélo* becomes *faire du vélo*. The topic exists because those contractions are in every sentence about what you do, because *fois* counts how often, and because *pour rester en forme* is the first *pour* plus infinitive most students write. Get the pairs right here and they are right for ever.

examples.title: Can you play it?
examples.body: The test is one question. Football, tennis, cards, video games: you can play them, so *jouer à*. Cycling, swimming, dancing, climbing: you do them, so *faire de*. *Faire au foot* and *jouer du vélo* are the errors an examiner sees most, and both come from not asking. The verb is chosen by the activity, not by the English, which uses *play* and *go* in ways French ignores.

examples.title: The contraction happens on its own
examples.body: *À* and *de* will not sit next to *le* or *les*: they fuse. *À le* is always *au*, *à les* is *aux*, *de le* is *du*, *de les* is *des*, while *la* and *l'* stay whole. The fusion is automatic, and a written *à le foot* is as visible as a spelling mistake. Four fused forms cover every sport and every activity you will ever name, and they turn up again with places, *au stade*, *à la piscine*.

examples.body: How often is *fois*: *une fois, deux fois par semaine, trois fois par mois*. It is not *temps*, which is time in general or the weather, and the confusion is the false friend this topic guards against. Add where, *à la piscine*, with whom, *avec mon équipe*, and why, *pour rester en forme*, and a sentence about sport has four pieces of detail, which is what a picture task or a listening question is fishing for.

steps.title: Jouer à et faire de
steps.body:
Sports and activities in French split into two families, and the verb tells you which.

**Jouer à** — games you *play*: *jouer au foot, au tennis, au basket, au rugby, à la pétanque, aux cartes, aux jeux vidéo*.

**Faire de** — activities you *do*: *faire du vélo, du ski, du jogging, de la natation, de la danse, de la gymnastique, de l'équitation, de l'escalade, des randonnées*.

The article changes because **à** and **de** contract with **le** and **les**:

- *à + le* → **au**, *à + les* → **aux**
- *de + le* → **du**, *de + les* → **des**
- *à la, à l', de la, de l'* stay as they are

So *le foot* gives *jouer **au** foot*, *les cartes* gives *jouer **aux** cartes*, *le vélo* gives *faire **du** vélo* and *la natation* gives *faire **de la** natation*. In a positive sentence the article is never left out, and it is never written as *à le* or *de le*.

***Faire* is irregular**: *je fais, tu fais, il/elle/on fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils/elles font*.

steps.title: Quand, et combien de fois ?
steps.body:
A good answer says **how often**, and this topic has its own way of counting.

**Fois** = times: *une fois par semaine* (once a week), *deux fois par semaine* (twice a week), *trois fois par mois*. Not *temps* — *temps* is time in general, *fois* is an occasion.

**When**: *le week-end, le samedi matin, après l'école, le soir, pendant les vacances, en été / en hiver* (in summer / in winter).

**Where**: *au parc, à la piscine* (swimming pool), *au stade, au gymnase, au centre sportif, à la montagne, dans un club*. The same *à + le = au* rule applies to places.

**With whom**: *avec mes amis, avec mon équipe* (team), *tout seul / toute seule* (on my own).

**Membership**: *je suis membre d'un club de natation. Je fais partie d'une équipe de foot.*

A sentence that stacks these is the target: *Je fais de la natation **deux fois par semaine, à la piscine, avec mon équipe**.* Twice a week for an hour is 8 hours across four weeks — a figure a reading text may expect you to work out.

steps.title: Il faut, and opinions
steps.body:
**Advice** about staying active uses **il faut** + infinitive: *il faut faire du sport, il faut bouger* (move), *il faut manger équilibré* (eat a balanced diet), *il faut boire de l'eau*. *Il ne faut pas rester devant l'écran toute la journée* (must not stay in front of the screen all day).

**Opinions** take the pattern from the opinions topic — verb + article + noun, or verb + infinitive: *j'adore le sport, je préfère la natation, j'aime faire du vélo, je déteste courir* (to run).

**Reasons**: *c'est bon pour la santé* (good for your health), *c'est amusant, c'est relaxant, ça me détend* (it relaxes me), *ça fait du bien* (it does you good), *c'est fatigant, c'est trop cher, c'est ennuyeux*.

**A negative habit** takes *ne … jamais de*: *je ne fais jamais de jogging*, *je ne joue jamais **au** foot* — note that after *jouer à* the article stays *au*, because the *de* rule only shrinks the indefinite and partitive articles *un / une / du / de la / des*.

**Extend** with *depuis* + time for how long you have done it: *je fais de la danse **depuis** trois ans* — present tense in French for something that started in the past and continues.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write *I play football* and *I go swimming*, choosing the right verb for each.
2. Write the six forms of *faire*.
3. Translate *three times a week*.

**Part B.**

4. Write where and with whom you do your sport, using *au / à la* for the place.
5. Say what sport you never do, and why.
6. Translate: *I do sport to stay fit.*

**Part C.**

7. Give two pieces of advice with *il faut*.
8. Say how long you have done your sport with *depuis*.
9. Write five sentences: what you do, how often and where, an opinion with a reason, something you never do, and advice.

For question 9, check every *à le* and *de le* — they should not exist.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Choose the verb by the activity.** *Jouer à* for games, *faire de* for activities. *Faire au foot* and *jouer du vélo* are the errors an examiner sees most, and the rule is one question: can you play it?

**Contract every time.** *Au, aux, du, des* — never *à le, à les, de le, de les*. *À la, à l', de la, de l'* stay whole. A Year 9 answer that gets every contraction right stands out immediately.

**Count with fois.** *Deux fois par semaine*, not *deux temps*. And stack the details: frequency, place, company, in one sentence.

**Know faire cold.** *Faisons, faites, font* are the three irregular forms; *vous faites* is the one most often written as *vous faisez*.

**Use pour + infinitive for the reason.** *Pour rester en forme, pour me détendre, pour être en bonne santé.* It turns *I do sport* into *I do sport in order to…* — purpose, which is a higher-band idea.

**Apply the de rule only where it belongs.** *Je ne fais jamais **de** natation* but *je ne joue jamais **au** foot*. Knowing where the rule stops shows you understand it.

**Add depuis.** *Je fais de la danse depuis trois ans* — present tense + *depuis* for something still going on. English uses *have been doing*; French does not, and using the present here is exactly right.

**Give advice with il faut.** *Il faut bouger tous les jours, il ne faut pas rester devant l'écran.* Impersonal, an infinitive after it, no conjugation to get wrong.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Jouer à** for games: *au foot, au tennis, aux cartes*.
- **Faire de** for activities: *du vélo, de la natation, de l'équitation, des randonnées*.
- **À + le = au, à + les = aux, de + le = du, de + les = des.**
- *La* and *l'* never contract.
- **Faire**: *fais, fais, fait, faisons, faites, font*.
- **Fois** counts times: *deux fois par semaine*.
- Where: *à la piscine, au stade, au parc*.
- With whom: *avec mon équipe, tout seul*.
- **Pour** + infinitive: *pour rester en forme*.
- Reasons: *c'est bon pour la santé, ça me détend*.
- **Ne … jamais de** shrinks *un / une / du / de la / des* only; *au* stays.
- **Depuis** + present tense: *depuis trois ans*.
- **Il faut** + infinitive for advice.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: **je fais partie d'une équipe de rugby et on s'entraîne le mercredi soir**.
options: I was part of a rugby team and we trained on Wednesday evenings.
I'm part of a rugby team and they train on Wednesday evenings.
I'm part of a rugby team and we train on Wednesday evenings.

questions.solution: **I'm part of a rugby team and we train on Wednesday evenings.** *Faire partie de* = to be part of; *s'entraîner* = to train; *le mercredi soir* = on Wednesday evenings, every week. The version with *was … trained* puts two present-tense verbs into the past; *they train* reads *on* as other people, when here it is the team the speaker belongs to; and *this Wednesday evening* misses that *le* + a day means every week.

examTechnique.body:
Pick **jouer à** for games and **faire de** for activities, and contract **au, aux, du, des** every time. Count with **fois**, and add a place with *au / à la* and company with *avec*.

Give an opinion with a reason, use **pour** + infinitive for why you do it, **depuis** + present for how long, and close with advice built on **il faut**.
examinerErrors: Writing à le or de le instead of au or du.
Using faire au or jouer du.
Conjugating vous faites as vous faisez.
Shrinking au to de after a negative.
Using a past tense with depuis.
Conjugating the verb after pour or il faut.
Giving an opinion with no reason.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer chooses **jouer à** or **faire de** correctly for every activity and contracts **au / aux / du / des** without a slip. It stacks frequency with *fois*, a place and a companion into one sentence, gives reasons with *c'est bon pour la santé* or *ça me détend*, and uses **pour** + infinitive for purpose. It knows the *de* rule shrinks *un / une / du / de la / des* but not *au*, uses **depuis** with the present tense, and gives advice with **il faut** + infinitive.
